clue.text: Is no longer interested in row, abandoned with gusto (8)

annotation.surface: Someone rows with gusto and then abandons the boat, or a quarrel conducted with wild enthusiasm.

annotation.definitionFit: To outgrow something is to lose interest in it as you mature, as a child outgrows toys.

clue.text: Clumsy pronouncement by easily surprised patron of seafood restaurant (6)

clue.text: Kettle, perhaps one that’ll leak (7-6)

clue.text: Starts to figure out problem? Dandy! (3)

indicators.note: the starts of the following words give the letters

annotation.walkthrough: 'Dandy!' reads as an old-fashioned exclamation meaning excellent; it is the noun, a vain dresser.
annotation.definitionFit: A fop is a dandy, a man overly concerned with his clothes.

clue.text: Falling apart with bile, pair of unionists: slow down there! (5-2,4)

annotation.surface: A political alliance of two unionists collapses in a fit of bile, with someone urging calm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Falling apart' reads as one phrase; only 'Falling' is the instruction and 'apart' is fodder. In Britain a built-up area has a lower speed limit, hence slow down.
annotation.definitionFit: Drivers must slow down in a built-up area, where lower speed limits apply.

clue.text: Pick up and convert this particular set piece (4,3,6)

the definite article singles out one particular thing
a corner kick is a set piece in football

annotation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'pick up' look like collecting the ball and 'convert' look like scoring, but pick up means improve.

annotation.walkthrough: 'Put on' in an across clue means placed after, so the tattoo sits to the right of the chest muscle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a spectator watches an event, from the Latin spectare, to look at.

blocks.note: having borrowed money, you owe it
